home.title: Craft Your Own Irrigation System
home.heroText: Discover the right method for your area and enjoy effortless automatic irrigation.

content.title: Drip Irrigation
content.description: Delivers water directly to the root zone through emitters or drip lines. Extremely water-efficient with minimal evaporation. Ideal for vegetable gardens, flower beds, shrubs, and greenhouses. Best choice for DIY systems focused on efficiency and control.

content.title: Micro Irrigation
content.description: Uses low-flow emitters or small spray heads at low pressure. Balances coverage and efficiency. Suitable for mixed plantings and landscaped areas. Commonly combined with drip systems.

content.title: Subsurface Irrigation
content.description: Water is delivered below the soil surface directly to roots. Very high efficiency with minimal evaporation. More complex installation and maintenance. Ideal for long-term, permanent installations.

content.title: Sprinkler Irrigation
content.description: Uses sprinklers or spray heads to distribute water over a larger area. Commonly used for lawns and open landscape areas. Easy to automate but less efficient due to wind drift and evaporation. Suitable for homeowners prioritizing uniform coverage.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: Our mission is to empower homeowners to confidently design, build, and maintain their own irrigation systems. We provide clear, practical education, proven methods, and reliable resources that make efficient irrigation accessible to everyone - regardless of prior technical experience. By promoting do-it-yourself solutions, smart water use, and long-term sustainability, we help people reduce costs, conserve water, and create healthier gardens and landscapes through systems they fully understand and control.

drip.name: Drip Irrigation
drip.headline: Water exactly where it is needed.
drip.description: A practical solution for vegetable gardens, flower beds, shrubs and greenhouses. Water reaches directly to the roots with minimal losses.
drip.comp5Desc: Close the end of the drip pipe
drip.step0: Plan the main pipe route from the water source to the beds and mark zone positions.
drip.step1: Install the filter and pressure reducer directly on the tap or start connector.
drip.step2: Lay the drip pipe along plant rows and secure with stakes every 50–80 cm.
drip.step3: Turn the system on and check for leaks. Set the timer for regular watering.
drip.sys0Desc: Ideal for a small vegetable garden or flower bed.
drip.sys1Desc: Covers a medium garden with several different zones.
drip.sys2Desc: For larger areas and greenhouses with multiple zones.
drip.faq0q: Can I install the system myself?
drip.faq0a: Yes. Drip irrigation is one of the most accessible for DIY installation. Most components connect without special tools. Follow our video tutorials for a step-by-step guide.
drip.faq1q: How much water does the system save compared to manual watering?
drip.faq1a: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the roots, without losses from evaporation or splashing. Typically 30–50 % water is saved compared to manual watering or sprinkler systems.
drip.faq2q: Can I connect it to a timer?
drip.faq2a: Yes — virtually any system can be equipped with a mechanical or digital timer. Timers allow automatic watering at set times without your presence.
drip.faq3a: Yes — drip irrigation is the preferred method in greenhouses because it keeps leaves dry and reduces the risk of fungal diseases.
drip.faq4q: How do I prevent clogging of the drippers?
drip.faq4a: Install a quality filter at the inlet and clean it regularly. With hard water, flushing the system at the end of the season is also recommended.
drip.ctaText: Use our calculator or contact our team for a free consultation.

micro.name: Micro Irrigation
micro.headline: Every pot gets its dose of water.
micro.description: A flexible solution for pots, small areas, terraces, hanging baskets and delicate plants.
micro.step0: Lay the main tube along the terrace or shelf, near all pots.
micro.step1: Install the filter and pressure reducer on the tap or supply hose.
micro.step2: Connect micro-tubes to the main tube and direct emitters into pots.
micro.step3: Check each pot receives the right amount of water and set the timer.
micro.sys0Desc: Perfect for a small terrace or window boxes.
micro.sys1Desc: Covers a larger terrace with different plant types.
micro.sys2Desc: For extensive green terraces, balconies or flower shops.
micro.faq0q: Can the system work with different types of pots?
micro.faq0a: Yes. Emitters can be placed in virtually any pot — from small window boxes to 50-litre planters. Flow is adjusted individually for each pot.
micro.faq1q: What is the maximum length of the main tube?
micro.faq1a: At standard pressure the main tube can be up to 15–20 m. For longer runs a larger diameter or additional supply point is required.
micro.faq2q: Does it work at low tap pressure?
micro.faq2a: Yes — micro systems are designed for low operating pressure (0.5–1.5 bar). The pressure reducer ensures correct operation even at higher mains pressure.
micro.faq3q: Can I add new pots later?
micro.faq3a: Yes. The main tube can be expanded with T-connectors and additional micro-tubes at any time.
micro.ctaText: Plan your system with our calculator or request a free consultation.

sprinkler.name: Sprinkler Irrigation
sprinkler.headline: Green lawn without moving the hose.
sprinkler.description: Uniform automated watering for turf areas with clean and full coverage.
sprinkler.step0: Prepare a zone plan by shape, slope and water needs. Confirm hydraulic calculations with an engineer.
sprinkler.step1: Dig trenches for underground pipes (≥ 20 cm deep). Lay pipes and connect valves.
sprinkler.step2: Install pop-up sprinklers at design positions and level with the ground surface.
sprinkler.step3: Connect the controller, program zones and carry out a test run. Adjust angles and radii.
sprinkler.sys0Desc: Ideal for a small rectangular lawn or yard.
sprinkler.sys1Desc: Covers a larger turf area with multiple zones.
sprinkler.sys2Desc: For large irregular areas with many zones.
sprinkler.faq0q: Do I need a specialist for installation?
sprinkler.faq0a: Unlike drip irrigation, sprinkler systems require excavation work and precise hydraulic calculations. We strongly recommend consulting our technical team before installation.
sprinkler.faq1q: Will the pipes and sprinklers be visible?
sprinkler.faq1a: Pipes are fully underground. Pop-up sprinklers rise only during active watering and retract below lawn level after each cycle.
sprinkler.faq2q: How does the system react to rain?
sprinkler.faq2a: We recommend installing a rain sensor that automatically blocks the cycle during rainfall. Modern smart controllers also integrate weather forecasts.
sprinkler.faq3a: It depends on the number of zones and sprinkler flow rate. Our calculator gives indicative values; exact data is obtained after hydraulic design.
sprinkler.faq4q: When is the best time to water?
sprinkler.faq4a: Early morning (5:00–9:00) is optimal — reduced evaporation, lower mains pressure and leaves dry before midday.
sprinkler.ctaText: Use our calculator for an indicative estimate or request full hydraulic design from our team.

subsurface.name: Subsurface Irrigation
subsurface.headline: Water delivered silently beneath the soil.
subsurface.description: Buried lateral pipes deliver water directly into the root zone, eliminating evaporation, surface runoff and weed stimulation. The ultimate method for crops, orchards, vineyards and sports turf.
subsurface.comp1Desc: Maintains steady low pressure in laterals
subsurface.comp2Desc: Conveys water from source to zone headers
subsurface.comp3Desc: Buried 15–45 cm, with in-line emitters every 30–50 cm
subsurface.comp4Desc: Prevent soil ingestion when system shuts off
subsurface.comp5Desc: Allow periodic flushing to remove sediment
subsurface.step0: Map the field, design lateral spacing (40–80 cm) and depth (20–35 cm) based on soil type and crop root depth. Consult a specialist for hydraulic design.
subsurface.step1: Use a vibrating shank or trencher to install laterals at the correct depth. Lay mainline headers in shallow trenches at field edges.
subsurface.step2: Connect laterals to zone headers with compression fittings. Install air-relief valves at high points and flush end caps at low ends.
subsurface.step3: Flush the system thoroughly. Conduct a pressure test, set controller programmes and check emitter uniformity with flow measurements.
subsurface.sys0Desc: Ideal for a kitchen garden, orchard row or demonstration strip.
subsurface.sys1Desc: Covers a commercial vegetable plot or small orchard with multiple zones.
subsurface.sys2Desc: Full-field SDI system for vineyards, sports pitches or intensive crops.
subsurface.faq0q: Can I install subsurface irrigation myself?
subsurface.faq0a: Small systems (up to ~500 m²) can be DIY-installed with a hand trencher or vibrating shank. Larger fields require specialist machinery and hydraulic design — we strongly recommend consulting our technical team.
subsurface.faq1q: How deep should the laterals be buried?
subsurface.faq1a: Typically 20–35 cm for vegetables and row crops, and 30–45 cm for orchards and vineyards. Depth depends on root profile, tillage depth and frost risk in your area.
subsurface.faq2q: How do I prevent root intrusion into emitters?
subsurface.faq2a: Use laterals with copper-impregnated anti-root emitters. Running a brief flush cycle after every irrigation helps clear the lines, and installing a check valve prevents soil ingestion when pressure drops.
subsurface.faq3q: How long does a subsurface system last?
subsurface.faq3a: Quality HDPE laterals with anti-root, anti-UV emitters can last 15–25 years with correct filtration, annual flushing and proper pressure management.
subsurface.faq4q: Can I use it for fertigation?
subsurface.faq4a: Yes — subsurface drip is ideal for fertigation because nutrients are delivered directly to the root zone with zero surface loss. A simple venturi or pump injector is all that is needed.
subsurface.ctaText: Plan your subsurface system with our calculator or request a full hydraulic design from our team.
